title: Machine learning discovers D-amino-acid mixtures that boost anti-biofilm antibiotic cocktails
summary: A machine-learning-guided high-throughput screen identified a five-component D-amino-acid mixture (“D-mix”) with about 78% anti-biofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa at 100 μM. Combining D-mix with half the lowest effective gentamicin dose retained about 91% bacterial-growth inhibition and about 93% anti-biofilm efficacy in vitro. In a small mouse lung-infection model, gentamicin/D-mix treatment reduced measured P. aeruginosa burden by about 95% in blood and 91% in lung tissue at 72 hours.
ai_technology: High-throughput screening coupled to machine-learning regression and iterative global optimization of D-amino-acid mixture ratios
organization: University of Science and Technology Beijing Institute for Advanced Materials and Technology; National Materials Corrosion and Protection Data Center; Beijing University of Chemical Technology

evidence.tested: In a small mouse lung-infection model, gentamicin/D-mix treatment reduced measured P. aeruginosa burden by about 95% in blood and 91% in lung tissue at 72 hours.
evidence.unknown: The in-vivo experiment used a small mouse P. aeruginosa infection model, not human treatment; study-specific bacterial counts and efficacy are reported at 72 hours. The composition is a selected mixture of five D-amino acids, with authors noting the full synergism mechanism remains unclear. D-mix alone was not bactericidal under the reported in-vitro conditions; effects are combination- and assay-dependent.
evidence.ai_role: Experimental measurements of mixture biofilm effects were used to train and iteratively update ML regression models, which guided mixture selection over design rounds. The selected D-mix was then evaluated with different antibiotics in vitro; the lead gentamicin/D-mix combination was tested in a P. aeruginosa lung-infection mouse model.
